digest.en: Russian strikes in Ukraine kill 10 as Zelensky claims Ukraine has hit oil tankers and terminals. Meanwhile, the US is set to cut troops in Germany amid escalating tensions with Iran, which has dismissed a potential US military operation as "impossible". Taiwan President Tsai Ing-wen begins a trip to Eswatini despite China's criticism.

articles.title: Russian strikes kill 10 as Zelensky says Ukraine hits oil tankers and terminal
articles.summary: Russian strikes in Ukraine killed 10 people, according to reports. Zelensky said Ukraine's drones hit Russian oil tankers and a terminal, but the extent of the damage is unclear. Fatalities have been reported around Ukraine as Kyiv says Russian "shadow fleet" tankers were hit by drones.

articles.title: Iran says U.S. military operation ‘impossible’ as Trump mulls peace proposal
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump faces a choice between a military operation deemed impossible by Iran's intelligence organisation and a peace proposal, according to a state television post. The Islamic Republic of Iran has presented a proposal to Trump, who must decide on a course of action.

articles.title: US to cut troops in Germany as Iran war spat deepens
articles.summary: The US plans to cut troops in Germany amid a deepening spat between President Trump and Chancellor Merz over the war on Iran. The move strains US-German relations, with tensions escalating between the two nations.

articles.title: Trump says he is likely to reject peace proposal as Iran has 'not yet paid a big enough price'
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has expressed doubts about an Iranian peace proposal, saying Iran has not yet paid a big enough price. Trump's comments suggest he may reject the proposal, which has been presented by the Iranian government.

articles.title: Iran presses for end to war within 30 days even as Trump expresses doubts
articles.summary: Iran's military has given the US 30 days to end the war, presenting two options: a military operation deemed impossible or a bad deal. The ultimatum comes as tensions between the two nations continue to escalate.

articles.title: Tallest for nearly 25 years, now ranked 25th
articles.summary: The Sears Tower, completed in 1973, held the title of world's tallest building for nearly 25 years before being surpassed. Now ranked 25th, the tower remains a notable landmark in Chicago, with its height still a subject of urban legend.

articles.title: Israel approves purchase of fighter jets from the US
articles.summary: Israel approved a purchase of F-35 and F-15IA fighter jets from Lockheed Martin and Boeing. Purchase includes two new combat squadrons of F-35 and F-15IA aircraft from Lockheed Martin and Boeing.

articles.title: Two US service members missing after military exercises in Morocco
articles.summary: Two US service members are missing in Morocco after military exercises near Tan Tan.

articles.summary: Iran has vowed to protect its nuclear stockpile despite Trump's threats. articles.title: The U.S. Set Off a Corruption Scandal That Is Gripping Mexico
articles.summary: A US indictment of a Mexican governor spotlighted cartel corruption in Mexico. The U. S. indictment of a Mexican governor has spotlighted cartel corruption, strained cross-border relations and handed President Claudia Sheinbaum a thorny choice.

articles.title: Global Demand for Rare Earth Minerals Is Intensifying Criminal Threats in the Amazon Rainforest
articles.summary: Global demand for rare earth minerals is driving criminal activity in the Amazon Rainforest, fueled by surging demand for critical minerals used in drones and electric cars. Global demand for critical minerals, used to build drones and electric cars, is surging, setting of a new wave of criminality in the world’s largest rainforest.

articles.title: Germany troop cuts send wrong signal to Russia, say two top US Republicans
articles.summary: Two top US Republicans say Germany's plan to cut 5,000 troops sends the wrong signal to Russia, risking deterrence. The chairs of the House and Senate armed services committees said withdrawing 5,000 service personnel risked undermining deterrence.

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh Asks Pro-Khalistanis Waving Flag At Canada Concert To Leave

articles.title: Man charged with murder of five-year-old girl whose death sparked riot
